newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Friday viewed as key for stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Friday viewed as key for stocks.

text.p: U.S. stocks extended their post-Greenspan rally Thursday, but options strategists said Friday would likely be a key to the market's longer term outlook.

Traders, investors and analysts will be watching the February U.S. employment report, due out before the market opens Friday, for any sign of rising inflation, which some believe could lead to an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.
"Tomorrow is going to be a tell-tale day the way I look at it," Jerry Hegarty at Thomson Financial Services said.
One indication that investor wariness ahead of the data had picked up was a rise in the Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index .VIX.
At about 1115 CST/1715 GMT, the VIX was up 0.85, or 3.95 percent, at 22.29. It had reached 22.49.
Some strategists see the VIX, calculated using certain S&P 100 index .OEX put and call prices, as a loose measure of investors' view of how much risk is in the market.
The VIX typically rises when the market falls, but it was up Thursday in the face of higher prices.
The bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI was up 35 points at 6,981, the S&P 500 index .SPX gained about half a point to 802.61 and the OEX rose 1.77 to 780.44.
Hegarty said the VIX was up mainly because of Friday's unemployment report.
"I would make more of it if tomorrow was a non-eventful day and there wasn't much going on," he said. "I think tomorrow the VIX will be down pretty good. It's temporarily inflated."
Todd Salamone, an analyst at Investment Research Institute, said OEX implied volatilities have not been at or near extreme levels.
"Implied volatilities on the puts is higher than in the calls, but that's been the case this whole bull market," he said. "In the past few days I haven't seen huge extremes."
He added that it appeared bond futures traders were expecting a negative surprise from the employment report, which sets the stage for a rally if the numbers are benign.
Hegarty said a stock market rally Friday would lead to a longer term rally.

"Tomorrow is a day where if they rally in the face of the unemployment report and (Federeal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's comments recently, you can take all the concerns and set them aside -- we're ready for another couple hundred points on the Dow," he explained.
"If tomorrow is a struggle, there are a couple different scenarios," he added. "One would call for slightly higher prices, and the other would call for a big decline.
